MSCI could drop Strategy and Metaplanet in November, but $3B sell-off fears overlook Strategy's trading volume

"There were some rumors that the MSCI may consider new ways to determine who qualifies to be in the index. And companies that don't have meaningful cash flows may be eliminated."

"Strategy and Metaplanet, they make their money or their balance sheet based on financial engineering and not an underlying operating business. And the MSCI is saying, we don't necessarily want that."

"The list is going to come out November 11th. We don't actually even know. And it would go into effect November 30th."

"The big story that you're reading about this is people saying that would mean a $3 billion dump of Strategy stock. It's all over. $3 billion dumping. Not even one trading day of Strategy stock, which is one of the most highly traded assets in the stock exchange. Not even a day of daily volume."

"Even if $3 billion was market dumped in a day, which is not how this would happen, it would slowly unwind and they would be eliminated. It would be a rounding error in the amount of trading that happens on Strategy stock on a daily basis."

"We have yet again managed to make a massive narrative out of something that's probably a mess. A rounding error."

zh_summary: @deepakshenoy建議印度央行從其660噸黃金中出售予黃金ETF並存於其金庫，贖回時再買回；這樣更便宜，並可減少黃金進口帶來的外匯需求。
en_summary: @deepakshenoy suggests the RBI sell gold from its 660 tons to Indian gold ETFs and keep it in its vaults, buying back on redemptions; this would be cheaper and reduce FX demand from gold imports.
ko_summary: @deepakshenoy는 인도중앙은행이 보유 금 660톤 중 일부를 금 ETF에 팔아 금고에 보관하고 환매 시 되사자고 제안했다. 더 저렴하고 금 수입에 따른 외환 수요를 줄인다.
text:
Interesting proposal. I believe it will help if rbi effectively sells gold to the etfs and sequesters them in its vaults. So if rbi have 660 tons of gold and etfs want 10 tons, rbi can sell it to them and mark it as such in the rbi vault. 

It will be cheaper and then rbi can always purchase the gold back when there is a redemption. This will also reduce total money in the system since rbi sells and takes out money from the system. 

Eventually it still has custody of the gold, doesn't have to worry about losing access to gold (it can always buy it back) and etf demand is totally fulfilled and safe. 

It will hurt gold vaults to some extent cos we will trust rbi vaults far more than private ones. It will reduce some physical import demand perhaps as etfs own about 120 tons of gold this far but it's growing. Rbi has 660.

My suggestion was that rbi sells gold to jewellers but this does something equivalent and probably better.

2026 has honestly felt like death by a thousand cuts for growth investors because every time we get through one macro shock another one seems to show up. 

The Iran war has pushed oil prices and yields higher creating another inflation shock that's making Fed's job even harder while many of the businesses I own continue executing despite their stock prices telling a very different story. 

I think this is where the emotional tax of long-term investing really shows up because patience feels easy when your stocks are making new highs but it becomes a completely different animal when those same companies are suddenly down 50% or more.

The irony to me is that everyone wants to own the company that becomes a 20-year winner but very few people actually want the 20-year ownership experience.

Those returns rarely come in a straight line and I think some of my best portfolio decisions are made during periods like this when everything feels uncomfortable but long -term opportunity really hasn't changed.

zh_summary: 在回調期間加倉 $ASTS，因為利率上升不會改變我們正處於建立更大型太空經濟的早期階段，衛星將成為全球電信基礎設施的另一層。AST 已與運營商建立合作，可觸及約30億潛在用戶，運營商有理由支持 Starlink 的替代方案，而非完全依賴 $SPCX 提供直連手機連接。目前最大挑戰是擴展至約45顆衛星並將合作轉為付費用戶，但股價已回調約70%，生產及發射風險已反映在估值中。
en_summary: Adding to $ASTS during drawdown as rising yields do not change how early we are in building a larger space economy with satellites as another layer of global telecom infrastructure. AST has carrier partnerships accessing ~3B potential subscribers who prefer an alternative to $SPCX Starlink for direct-to-phone. Challenge is scaling to ~45 satellites and converting to paying users, but ~70% drawdown already reflects production and launch risk in valuation.
ko_summary: 조정 기간에 $ASTS 포지션을 늘리고 있다. 금리 상승은 우리가 더 큰 우주 경제를 구축하는 초기 단계이며 위성이 글로벌 통신 인프라의 또 다른 층이 된다는 사실을 바꾸지 않기 때문이다. AST는 이미 운용사 파트너십으로 약 30억 잠재 가입자에게 접근할 수 있으며, 운용사들은 $SPCX Starlink에 완전히 의존하기보다 대안을 지원할 이유가 충분하다. 현재 최대 과제는 약 45개 위성으로 확장하고 파트너십을 유료 사용자로 전환하는 것이지만, 주가가 이미 약 70% 조정되어 생산 및 발사 리스크가 밸류에이션에 반영되었다고 본다.
text:
I've been adding to my $ASTS position during this drawdown because rising yields don't change how early we are in building a much larger space economy where satellites become another layer of global telecom infrastructure.

AST already has carrier partnerships giving it access to ~3B potential subscribers and those carriers have every reason to support an alternative to Starlink rather than depend entirely on $SPCX for direct-to-phone connectivity.

The biggest challenge now is scaling to ~45 satellites and turning those partnerships into paying users but with the stock already in a ~70% drawdown I do think a lot of that production and launch risk is being reflected in valuation.

In advanced economies, interest payments now consume 9.5% of government tax revenues. Between 2011 and 2019, that figure averaged just 6%.

These are IMF figures, and they directly affect your wallet and your wealth.

A recent article in the Netherlands’ leading financial newspaper discusses how governments and central banks can stop these interest costs from spiraling further out of control.

The newspaper calls it “a backdoor escape from the debt mountain.”

But “backdoor escape” doesn’t begin to capture what’s really happening. It’s a direct assault on the purchasing power of every household.

The escape route is more like sailing between Scylla and Charybdis: artificially low interest rates and higher inflation. Low rates keep government debt manageable. Higher inflation erodes its real value.

But this "backdoor" comes at a price.

Did you know that savings have lost 26% of their purchasing power over the past 25 years? More than a quarter of your wealth,  gone, just like that.

And did you know that those supposedly safe government bonds, a fixed component of virtually every diversified investment portfolio, have also destroyed purchasing power over the same period?

You read that right. Lending your hard-earned money to the government, trusting it to put that money to good use, has cost you purchasing power.

So forget the backdoor escape. Call it what it really is: a silent killer of your purchasing power.

And that’s exactly why we invest differently.

text:
AI stocks have sold off over the past few days.

The main drivers: hotter-than-expected US inflation (Sept CPI 3.7% YoY) raising the odds of further Fed hikes, plus growing worries about the cost of financing the massive AI infrastructure buildout. Heavily leveraged names like CoreWeave (roughly $50B in debt/obligations) have been hit especially hard, with bond yields spiking toward 15-16% and credit spreads flashing stress.

Yet the demand picture looks different. Cloud GPU rental prices for high-end chips remain elevated and in several cases, are still trending higher - a real-time signal that compute demand is tight. 

Meanwhile, OpenAI and Anthropic continue scaling: Anthropic just reported $16.8B in Q3 revenue (+45% QoQ), +ve FCF and adjusted profitability, while OpenAI’s net annualised run rate sits around $50B with strong enterprise growth.

This looks more like a rates-and-financing-driven valuation reset than a collapse in underlying AI demand. For investors who believe the secular compute story remains intact, these pullbacks can create selective opportunities - particularly in higher-quality names.

zh_summary: Ross Hendricks質疑市場為何專注於$CRWV即將崩潰，比較互聯網泡沫高峯期$CSCO約10%收入來自循環供應商融資交易，導致增長從+66%轉為-30%、股價跌80%，拖累納指跌80%。$CRWV約佔$NVDA GPU銷售的8%；失去新雲公司將摧毀$NVDA增長及AI資本支出交易，解釋$CAT $GEV $MU $AVGO $NVDA的慘況為債務驅動循環資本支出泡沫終結的開始。
en_summary: Ross Hendricks questions why the market is fixated on $CRWV's imminent demise, comparing to $CSCO at Dot Com peak which had 10% revenue from circular vendor-financed deals, leading to growth from +66% to -30% and 80% stock drop, dragging Nasdaq down 80%. $CRWV makes up roughly 8% of $NVDA GPU sales; losing neoclouds would nuke $NVDA growth and AI capex trade, explaining carnage in $CAT $GEV $MU $AVGO $NVDA as start of debt-fueled circular capex bubble end.
ko_summary: Ross Hendricks는 시장이 $CRWV의 임박한 붕괴에 왜 집착하는지 질문하며, 닷컴 버블 정점의 $CSCO가 순환 벤더 금융 거래에서 매출의 약 10%를 얻었고 성장이 +66%에서 -30%로, 주가가 80% 하락하며 나스닥을 80% 끌어내렸다고 비교했다. $CRWV는 $NVDA GPU 판매의 약 8%를 차지; 네오클라우드를 잃으면 $NVDA 성장과 AI 자본 지출 거래를 파괴하여 $CAT $GEV $MU $AVGO $NVDA의 학살을 부채 기반 순환 자본 지출 버블 종료의 시작으로 설명한다.
text:
Why is the overall market so fixated on $CRWV's imminent demise?

At the peak of the Dot Com bubble, $CSCO - the largest company in the world, and the $NVDA equivalent of the era - generated about 10% of its revenue from circular deals through vendor-financed startups. 

When those startups lost access to capital, $CSCO's revenue growth went from +66% to -30% within a few quarters, and the stock lost 80% of its value. The same story played out across the dot com supply chain, sending the Nasdaq down 80%.  

Today, $CRWV alone makes up roughly 8% of
$NVDA GPU sales. Losing that demand is enough to nuke $NVDA's growth story all by itself. 

Oh, and $CRWV isn't an isolated example - every major neocloud is hemmoraghing cash and borrowing costs are going UP across the board. 

If you lose the neoclouds, you lose the incremental growth driver for marginal data center capacity, and the AI capex trade goes up in smoke.

That's why we're seeing carnage across the entire AI supply chain, from $CAT and $GEV to $MU, $AVGO and more recently $NVDA.

en_summary: $SPCX is valued at ~$2T versus ~$35B for $RKLB which is ~60x higher despite generating only ~25x revenue with Rocket Lab trading at less than half sales multiple while still growing 62%. The market may be underappreciating Rocket Lab's Space Systems business, and if Neutron flies in 2027 the valuation gap could narrow.

text:
$SPCX is valued at ~$2T versus ~$35B for $RKLB which is ~60x higher despite generating only ~25x revenue with Rocket Lab trading at less than half sales multiple while still growing 62%.

I totally understand how SpaceX deserves a premium for Starlink, AI and its launch dominance but Rocket Lab already has a Space Systems business selling satellites and components across the industry which I think the market is absolutely underappreciating.

And if Neutron starts flying in 2027 then Rocket Lab becomes an even stronger alternative for both launch and spacecraft which is why I think valuation gap could narrow significantly as execution catches up.

en_summary: aleabitoreddit discusses laser suppliers for Ayar Labs, noting original disclosures of $LITE, $MTSI, and $SIVE, with analysis of their capabilities for new designs, multi-vendor approach, and timelines for 2027 production, concluding no assumptions can be made yet pending earnings.

text:
Nobody said $SIVE was going to be the sole laser provider for Ayar for all generations. 2nd gen Supernova was 16x wavelength that they confirmed Sivers.

Ayar is expected to do multi-vendor for lasers, would be stupid not to. Originally disclosed suppliers were $LITE, $MTSI, and $SIVE, but there's probably only a few companies that can do this new design. 

For their new demonstration at OCP it's 8x 200mW range, $LITE is probably the closest one technologically to Ayar's OCP announcement, with 8x 250 mW demonstrated at ECOC just last month that they're targeting availability later in 2027. 

I don't see anything where $MTSI has demonstrated remotely similar capabilities yet. Macom were saying they were still working on 75 mW qualifications targeting production H2 2027. 

$SIVE has lower power 8/16 channel specs, and individual 200 mW lasers for NPO. I think this might relate to their Seminex partnership for UHP multi channel variants that they were targeting for 2027 so high confidence they'll meet technology specs eventually, more of a matter of timing. 

But basically new announced configuration from Ayar, can't really make any assumptions here yet, will need to wait for earnings of these players.
